verdict.rationale: The axis applies, since a Python agent-orchestration framework could plausibly offer typed state schemas and build-time validation. The pack shows none: the only related item is that graph compilation runs "a few basic checks on the structure of your graph (no orphaned nodes, etc)". That is a structural check, not strict typing or schema validation of state or tool inputs. Nothing documents typed state schemas, validation, or static type-checking that would let a coding agent catch its own mistakes at build time.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can rely on strict typing and schema validation so a coding agent catches its own mistakes at build time
